262	# How this program reports what it found
263	
264	This worktree is the **report repository**. The code under review is the **target tree**, which is somewhere else on this host: `target.json` beside this file states its absolute path, the files it covers, and the SHA-256 the whole tree locks to.
265	
266	The target is read-only for every session of this program. `verify-safety-report.mjs` re-hashes every locked file on every run, so a target a department edited fails the program instead of releasing a report about a tree that no longer exists.
267	
268	## This file and the skills
269	
270	When the deployment mounts the code-safety knowledge pack, its `review-method`, `severity-and-evidence` and `report-template` skills own the craft: how to read a codebase, how to score a severity, what evidence has to name, and how the report reads. Follow them.
271	
272	This file owns what `verify-safety-report.mjs` mechanically decides, and it is binding wherever the two differ in form. There is one such place and it is stated below: the counts each summary carries are written as `- <severity>: <count>` lines so the examiner can compare them with the union, which is the machine-readable form of the skill's "counts per severity".
273	
274	## What a department delivers
275	
276	Two files, both committed on the department's own branch:
277	
278	- `findings/<department>.json` — a JSON array of findings, `[]` when the department found nothing.
279	- `report/<department>.md` — the department's own prose: what it looked at, what it found, and what it did not reach.
280	
281	Nothing else. Do not write `SAFETY-REPORT.md`, `findings.json`, `target.json` or `verify-safety-report.mjs`: the first two are the integration's, and the last two are the examiner.
282	
283	## The evidence rule
284	
285	A finding without a file and a line is not a finding. Quote the exact line you cite; `verify-safety-report.mjs` compares your `snippet` with the target's own text at that line, ignoring only whitespace, and refuses the whole file when they differ.
286	
287	Prefer three findings you have read the code for over twelve a pattern matched. `confidence` is what you actually know: `confirmed` when you read the sink, the source and the path between them; `likely` when the sink is dangerous and the source is plausibly attacker-controlled; `possible` when the pattern is there and the reachability is not established.
288	
289	## The finding
290	
291	```json
292	{
293	  "id": "secrets-cookie-secret",
294	  "cwe": "CWE-798",
295	  "owasp": "A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures",
296	  "severity": "high",
297	  "confidence": "confirmed",
298	  "title": "Session cookie secret is hard-coded in the committed configuration",
299	  "file": "config/env/all.js",
300	  "line": 8,
301	  "snippet": "cookieSecret: \"session_cookie_secret_key_here\",",
302	  "evidence": "The value is a literal in a committed file and is the secret express-session is configured with.",
303	  "impact": "Anyone with the repository can forge a session cookie and authenticate as any user.",
304	  "fix": "Read the secret from the environment and rotate the committed value.",
305	  "references": ["https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html"]
306	}
307	```
308	
309	| Field | Rule |
310	| --- | --- |
311	| `id` | letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, unique across the whole program; prefix it with your department or use the pack's `SEC-<n>` numbering. |
312	| `cwe` | `CWE-<number>`. |
313	| `owasp` | the OWASP Top 10 category, named. |
314	| `severity` | `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low` or `info`. |
315	| `confidence` | `confirmed`, `likely` or `possible`. |
316	| `title` | one line a reader can act on. |
317	| `file` | path relative to the target root, exactly as `target.json` lists it. |
318	| `line` | 1-based line in that file. |
319	| `endLine` | optional last line when the finding spans several; `snippet` then quotes all of them. |
320	| `snippet` | the target's own text at those lines, verbatim. |
321	| `evidence` | why this line is the vulnerability, naming what you read. |
322	| `impact` | what an attacker gets. |
323	| `fix` | what to change. |
324	| `references` | array of URLs or identifiers; may be empty. |
325	
326	## Checking your own work before you commit
327	
328	```sh
329	node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings findings/<department>.json
330	```
331	
332	That is the same command your goal is measured by. Run it, fix what it names, then commit everything — work left uncommitted is not delivered and is not measured.
333	
334	## What the integration delivers
335	
336	The integration merges every department branch and then writes two files of its own.
337	
338	`findings.json` is the union of every `findings/<department>.json`, deduplicated by `file` + `line` + `cwe`, keeping the entry with the higher `confidence`. Before writing it, ask the examiner which findings do not hold:
339	
340	```sh
341	for f in findings/*.json; do node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings "$f" --list-invalid; done
342	```
343	
344	Every id that command prints is dropped from `findings.json` and named under `## What was not covered`, with the reason the examiner gave. Dropping one silently fails the report: `--report` refuses a union that omits an id no section discloses.
345	
346	`SAFETY-REPORT.md` carries exactly these sections, in this order:
347	
348	```markdown
349	## Résumé exécutif
350	
351	<deux paragraphes en français : ce qui a été examiné, ce qui a été trouvé, ce que cela implique>
352	
353	- critical: 0
354	- high: 0
355	- medium: 0
356	- low: 0
357	- info: 0
358	
359	## Executive summary
360	
361	<the same in English>
362	
363	- critical: 0
364	- high: 0
365	- medium: 0
366	- low: 0
367	- info: 0
368	
369	## Scope and method
370	
371	<the target, its locked file count, which departments ran, which tools ran — the scanner, the advisory source — and which files were actually read>
372	
373	## Findings
374	
375	### critical
376	
377	- `<id>` — <title> (`<file>:<line>`, <cwe>, <confidence>) — <impact, then fix>
378	
379	### high
380	
381	...
382	
383	## What was not covered
384	
385	- <a department, a file kind, a class of vulnerability, or a check that did not run, and why>
386	- <every dropped finding id, with the examiner's reason>
387	
388	## Certificate
389	
390	Verified findings: <count>
391	Target tree: <the sha256 from target.json>
392	
393	<one sentence on what was checked mechanically: that every finding resolves to a real file and line in the locked tree, that every id is unique, and that no two findings share file, line and CWE>
394	
395	This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".
396	```
397	
398	Both summary sections state a `- <severity>: <count>` line for all five severities, and the five counts must be the counts `findings.json` actually holds. Every finding id in `findings.json` is cited in `## Findings`. Every `<file>:<line>` written anywhere in the report must resolve in the target, so write a path you did not read as prose rather than as a citation.
399	
400	The report is a review by a language model, grounded by a static scanner and by this examiner. Say so in `## Scope and method`. Never write that the target is secure, safe, or free of vulnerabilities: `verify-safety-report.mjs` refuses those claims, because nothing this program did could support one.
401	
402	Check it before you commit:
403	
404	```sh
405	node verify-safety-report.mjs --report
406	```

453	/** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
454	const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
455	
456	/** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
457	const PLACEHOLDER = /\bTODO\b|\bTBD\b|\bFIXME\b|lorem ipsum|<placeholder>|PLACEHOLDER/i
458	
459	/** String fields every finding states in prose. */
460	const PROSE_FIELDS = ['title', 'evidence', 'impact', 'fix']
461	
462	/** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
463	const normalize = (text) => text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
464	
465	/** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
466	const sha256 = (content) => createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
467	
468	/**
469	 * Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
470	 * @param {string} root directory to walk
471	 * @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
472	 * @returns {string[]} relative POSIX-ish paths, sorted
473	 */
474	function walk(root, exclude) {
475	  const found = []
476	  const descend = (directory) => {
477	    for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
478	      const path = join(directory, entry.name)
479	      if (entry.isDirectory()) {
480	        if (!exclude.includes(entry.name)) descend(path)
481	      } else if (entry.isFile()) found.push(relative(root, path))
482	    }
483	  }
484	  descend(root)
485	  return found.sort()
486	}
487	
488	/** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
489	class Target {
490	  /**
491	   * @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
492	   * @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
493	   */
494	  constructor(reportRoot, failures) {
495	    this.failures = failures
496	    this.root = undefined
497	    this.files = new Map()
498	    this.lines = new Map()
499	    const lockPath = join(reportRoot, 'target.json')
500	    if (!existsSync(lockPath)) {
501	      failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
502	      return
503	    }
504	    const lock = JSON.parse(readFileSync(lockPath, 'utf8'))
505	    this.root = lock.root
506	    this.exclude = lock.exclude ?? []
507	    this.digest = lock.sha256
508	    for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
509	    this.checkTree()
510	  }
511	
512	  /**
513	   * Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
514	   * cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
515	   * department edited is no longer that tree.
516	   */
517	  checkTree() {
518	    if (!existsSync(this.root)) {
519	      this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
520	      this.root = undefined
521	      return
522	    }
523	    const present = walk(this.root, this.exclude)
524	    for (const path of present) {
525	      if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
526	    }
527	    for (const [path, hash] of this.files) {
528	      if (!present.includes(path)) {
529	        this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
530	        continue
531	      }
532	      if (sha256(readFileSync(join(this.root, path))) !== hash) {
533	        this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
534	      }
535	    }
536	  }
537	
538	  /**
539	   * The lines of one target file.
540	   * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
541	   * @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
542	   */
543	  linesOf(path) {
544	    if (this.root === undefined || !this.files.has(path)) return undefined
545	    if (!this.lines.has(path)) this.lines.set(path, readFileSync(join(this.root, path), 'utf8').split('\n'))
546	    return this.lines.get(path)
547	  }
548	
549	  /**
550	   * Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
551	   * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
552	   * @param {number} line 1-based line number
553	   * @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
554	   */
555	  resolves(path, line) {
556	    const lines = this.linesOf(path)
557	    return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
558	  }
559	}
560	
561	/**
562	 * Decide one finding against the target tree.
563	 * @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
564	 * @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
565	 * @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
566	 * @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
567	 * @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
568	 */
569	function checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen) {
570	  const failures = []
571	  if (finding === null || typeof finding !== 'object' || Array.isArray(finding)) {
572	    return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
573	  }
574	  const id = finding.id
575	  const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
576	  const fail = (rule) => void failures.push(`${name}: ${rule}`)
577	  // Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
578	  // numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
579	  if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
580	  else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
581	  else seen.add(id)
582	  if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
583	  if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
584	  if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
585	  if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
586	  for (const field of PROSE_FIELDS) {
587	    if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
588	  }
589	  if (!Array.isArray(finding.references) || finding.references.some(reference => typeof reference !== 'string')) {
590	    fail('references must be an array of strings')
591	  }
592	  const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
593	  if (typeof file !== 'string' || file === '' || file.startsWith('/') || file.split('/').includes('..')) {
594	    fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
595	    return failures
596	  }
597	  const lines = target.linesOf(file)
598	  if (lines === undefined) {
599	    fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
600	    return failures
601	  }
602	  if (!Number.isInteger(line) || line < 1 || line > lines.length) {
603	    fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
604	    return failures
605	  }
606	  const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
607	  if (!Number.isInteger(last) || last < line || last > lines.length) {
608	    fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
609	    return failures
610	  }
611	  if (typeof snippet !== 'string' || snippet.trim() === '') {
612	    fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
613	    return failures
614	  }
615	  const quoted = normalize(lines.slice(line - 1, last).join('\n'))
616	  if (normalize(snippet) !== quoted) {
617	    fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
618	  }
619	  return failures
620	}
621	
622	/**
623	 * Read one findings file.
624	 * @param {string} path the file to read
625	 * @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
626	 * @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
627	 */
628	function readFindings(path, failures) {
629	  if (!existsSync(path)) {
630	    failures.push(`${path} is missing`)
631	    return []
632	  }
633	  let parsed
634	  try {
635	    parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
636	  } catch (error) {
637	    failures.push(`${path} is not JSON: ${error.message}`)
638	    return []
639	  }
640	  if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
641	    failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
642	    return []
643	  }
644	  return parsed
645	}
646	
647	/**
648	 * Decide one findings file on its own.
649	 * @param {string} path the findings file
650	 * @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
651	 * @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
652	 */
653	function checkFindingsFile(path, target) {
654	  const failures = []
655	  const findings = readFindings(path, failures)
656	  const invalid = []
657	  const seen = new Set()
658	  findings.forEach((finding, index) => {
659	    const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
660	    if (broken.length === 0) return
661	    failures.push(...broken.map(rule => `${basename(path)}: ${rule}`))
662	    invalid.push(typeof finding?.id === 'string' ? finding.id : `#${index + 1}`)
663	  })
664	  return { failures, invalid, findings }
665	}
666	
667	/**
668	 * The body of one section of the report.
669	 * @param {string} text the whole report
670	 * @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
671	 * @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
672	 */
673	function section(text, heading) {
674	  const start = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
675	  if (start === -1) return ''
676	  const body = text.slice(start + heading.length + 1)
677	  const next = body.search(/^## /m)
678	  return next === -1 ? body : body.slice(0, next)
679	}
680	
681	/**
682	 * Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
683	 * @param {string} root the report repository
684	 * @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
685	 * @returns {string[]} every rule the report broke
686	 */
687	function checkReport(root, target) {
688	  const reportPath = join(root, 'SAFETY-REPORT.md')
689	  if (!existsSync(reportPath)) {
690	    return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
691	  }
692	  const text = readFileSync(reportPath, 'utf8')
693	  const failures = []
694	  let previous = -1
695	  for (const heading of SECTIONS) {
696	    const at = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
697	    if (at === -1) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has no section ${JSON.stringify(heading)}`)
698	    else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
699	    else previous = at
700	  }
701	  const placeholder = PLACEHOLDER.exec(text)
702	  if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
703	  const overclaim = OVERCLAIMS.exec(text)
704	  if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
705	
706	  const union = checkFindingsFile(join(root, 'findings.json'), target)
707	  failures.push(...union.failures)
708	  const findings = union.findings.filter(finding => typeof finding?.id === 'string')
709	
710	  const keys = new Set()
711	  for (const finding of findings) {
712	    const key = `${finding.file}:${finding.line}:${finding.cwe}`
713	    if (keys.has(key)) failures.push(`findings.json states ${key} twice; the union is deduplicated by file, line and cwe`)
714	    keys.add(key)
715	  }
716	
717	  const listed = section(text, '## Findings')
718	  for (const finding of findings) {
719	    if (!listed.includes(finding.id)) failures.push(`the Findings section does not cite ${finding.id}`)
720	  }
721	  // The lookbehind keeps a URL's `host:port` out of the citation vocabulary:
722	  // the host is preceded by a slash, so no citation ever starts there.
723	  for (const [, path, line] of text.matchAll(/(?<![\w/.\-])([\w.-]+(?:\/[\w.-]+)*\.\w+):(\d+)\b/g)) {
724	    if (!target.resolves(path, Number(line))) failures.push(`the citation ${path}:${line} does not resolve in the tree under review`)
725	  }
726	
727	  const counts = Object.fromEntries(SEVERITIES.map(severity => [severity, findings.filter(finding => finding.severity === severity).length]))
728	  for (const heading of ['## Résumé exécutif', '## Executive summary']) {
729	    const body = section(text, heading)
730	    for (const severity of SEVERITIES) {
731	      const stated = new RegExp(`^- ${severity}: (\\d+)$`, 'm').exec(body)
732	      if (stated === null) failures.push(`${heading} does not state a "- ${severity}: <count>" line`)
733	      else if (Number(stated[1]) !== counts[severity]) {
734	        failures.push(`${heading} states ${severity}: ${stated[1]}, and findings.json holds ${counts[severity]}`)
735	      }
736	    }
737	  }
738	
739	  const uncovered = section(text, '## What was not covered')
740	  const department = join(root, 'findings')
741	  const dropped = []
742	  if (existsSync(department)) {
743	    for (const entry of readdirSync(department).sort()) {
744	      if (!entry.endsWith('.json')) continue
745	      for (const finding of readFindings(join(department, entry), failures)) {
746	        if (typeof finding?.id !== 'string') continue
747	        if (!findings.some(kept => kept.id === finding.id)) dropped.push(finding.id)
748	      }
749	    }
750	  }
751	  for (const id of dropped) {
752	    if (!uncovered.includes(id)) {
753	      failures.push(`${id} was dropped from findings.json and is not disclosed under "## What was not covered"`)
754	    }
755	  }
756	
757	  const certificate = section(text, '## Certificate')
758	  if (!certificate.includes(HONESTY)) failures.push(`the Certificate must state, verbatim: ${JSON.stringify(HONESTY)}`)
759	  const stated = /^Verified findings: (\d+)$/m.exec(certificate)
760	  if (stated === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Verified findings: <count>" line')
761	  else if (Number(stated[1]) !== findings.length) failures.push(`the Certificate states ${stated[1]} verified findings, and findings.json holds ${findings.length}`)
762	  const tree = /^Target tree: ([0-9a-f]{64})$/m.exec(certificate)
763	  if (tree === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Target tree: <sha256>" line')
764	  else if (tree[1] !== target.digest) failures.push(`the Certificate states target tree ${tree[1]}, and target.json locks ${target.digest}`)
765	  return failures
766	}
767	
768	const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
769	const root = resolve(process.cwd())
770	const listInvalid = argv.includes('--list-invalid')
771	const findingsAt = argv.indexOf('--findings')
772	const failures = []
773	const target = new Target(root, failures)
774	
775	if (findingsAt !== -1) {
776	  const path = argv[findingsAt + 1]
777	  if (path === undefined) {
778	    console.error('FAIL --findings needs a path')
779	    process.exit(1)
780	  }
781	  const checked = checkFindingsFile(resolve(root, path), target)
782	  if (listInvalid) {

785	  }
786	  failures.push(...checked.failures)

788	  // section: requiring a finding would buy one by inventing it.
789	  if (failures.length === 0) console.log(`ok: ${checked.findings.length} findings verified against ${target.root}`)

796	}
797	
798	if (failures.length > 0) {
799	  for (const failure of failures) console.error(`FAIL ${failure}`)

801	}

content.text:
## Rehearsal Report: Code-Safety POC Demo (fresh clone)

**Scope confirmed safe:** `/home/user/deepseek-harness` was never modified. Its head (`023d7c611550b74b7cb56c9fba7492c4e28955c1`) and branch are unchanged; its feed (PIDs 4256/4285, port 4711) and deck (PIDs 4310/4311, port 3000) were confirmed running with the **same PIDs and start times** before and after this rehearsal. All work happened in a separate clone at `/tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/wave2-rehearsal/fresh` on spare ports 4713/3013.

### What the runbook tells a user to do (step 2)
- `docs/code-safety-poc.md`: clone → `git checkout claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt` → `pnpm install` → `pnpm run build:lib:host` → `claude --version` → install semgrep into a venv and symlink it → clone NodeGoat → rehearse `pnpm run poc` + `pnpm run code-safety -- ~/targets/NodeGoat --model sonnet`.
- Root `README.md` "Code safety" section gives the same two commands.
- `apps/command-deck/README.md` documents the deck alone (`pnpm run deck`, build+start, fixtures snapshot) and the feed contract/replay behavior.
- `scripts/poc-demo.ts`: builds the deck (forced whenever `.next` is missing, or a non-default `--feed-port`), starts the feed, waits up to 90s for `/roster`, then starts `next start` for the deck; one SIGINT/SIGTERM stops both via their own process groups.
- `scripts/code-safety.ts` usage line (not in the runbook or README at all): `pnpm run code-safety -- <target path> [--out <dir>] [--model sonnet|opus] [--keyless]`.
- On this host, `claude --version` → `2.1.278 (Claude Code)` and `semgrep --version` → `1.177.0` are both already present (not a gap, just confirmed).

### Commands run, with timings and exit codes
| Step | Command | Time | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disk check | `df -h /tmp /home`; `du -sh node_modules` | — | 18G free (of 252G), main checkout `node_modules` = 1.8G — pass |
| Clone | `git clone --branch claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt /home/user/deepseek-harness .../fresh` | 1m15.8s | 0 |
| Install (offline) | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` | 7.6s | 0 |
| Build | `pnpm run build:lib:host` | 1m47.7s | 0 |
| Launch | `pnpm run poc -- --feed-port 4713 --deck-port 3013` (backgrounded) | ~89s to both ports answering (includes the forced deck build) | running, then 130 on SIGINT |
| Screenshots (LIVE) | `node shoot-live.mjs .../shots 1600 1000 "enterprise::…::9000" "process::…::12000" "safety::…::9000"` | 43.0s | 0 |
| Badge check (LIVE) | `node shoot-live-badge.mjs .../shots-badge 1600 1000 "enterprise::…::9000"` | ~9s | 0 |
| Screenshot (REPLAY) | `node shoot-replay-4713.mjs .../shots-replay 1600 1000 "replay::http://localhost:3013/::9000"` | ~9s | 0 |
| Shutdown | `kill -INT 6883` (the node process actually running `scripts/poc-demo.ts -- --feed-port 4713 --deck-port 3013`) | teardown complete in <2s | launcher exited 130 |
| Keyless (custom target) | `pnpm run code-safety -- .../fresh/packages/util --out .../keyless-run --keyless` | 37s wall (driver: 5s) | 1 (failed) |
| Keyless (sample-target, confirmation) | `pnpm run code-safety -- --out .../keyless-run-sampletarget --keyless` | 10.6s wall (driver: 5s) | 0 (released) |
| Cleanup | removed `fresh/node_modules` (1.8G) + `fresh/apps/command-deck/.next` (175M) | — | freed ~2GB; 17G still free |

**Head hash:** `023d7c611550b74b7cb56c9fba7492c4e28955c1` (exact match, both clones).

**Offline install:** worked (7.6s), but this host's pnpm store was already warm from the main checkout's own prior install — this does **not** prove a genuinely new laptop (empty store) can install without network; that laptop's first `pnpm install` will need network regardless of `--offline`. Two harmless postinstall warnings appeared either way (`ENOENT` creating bin symlinks for `dsh-acp-demo` and `dsh-sdk-jsonrpc-demo` — unrelated example demo bins, expected before `lib/` is built).

### LIVE mode (step 6)
Roster: `{"counts":{"defined":147,"active":0}}`, 147 agents, 10 divisions, 124 edges — exact match to documentation. Deck answered 200 on `/`, `/process`, `/safety`. Badge = `"live"`, footer = `feed http://localhost:4713·stream open·run 2026-09-19-nodegoat-2·…`.

Screenshots at `.../wave2-rehearsal/shots/{enterprise,process,safety}.png`:
- **enterprise.png** — the 147-agent nebula graph clustered into 10 colored division blobs (Harness Core, Code Safety, Knowledge, Governance, etc.) with delegation edges; right panel lists each division's agent count/purpose and a live event feed from run `2026-09-19-nodegoat-2`.
- **process.png** — six department lanes as glowing rails passing through three translucent gates (Verification, Judging, Integration); side panel shows the same run completed in 20m25s, 404/404 events, per-lane counts, and a scrolling event stream.
- **safety.png** — the reviewed NodeGoat tree as a lit 3D "code city," with light beams (findings) rising from files sized/colored by severity; right panel shows 111 files, 5 languages, 38 findings in a filterable table.

### REPLAY fallback (step 7)
With `localhost:4713` blocked at the network layer: badge = `"replay"`, footer = `feed http://localhost:4713·stream open·run 2026-09-19-nodegoat-2·— events/min·replaying committed fixtures — feed unreachable`. Screenshot (`.../shots-replay/replay.png`) shows the amber REPLAY badge plus an "Example data" callout: *"The feed at http://localhost:4713 is not answering, so the deck is replaying the fixtures committed with it. Nothing on screen comes from a live run."* Matches the documented behavior exactly.

### SIGINT shutdown (step 8)
Process tree matched the source comment exactly: `sh(6866)→node tsx-cli(6867)→node/tsx-loader(6883, running poc-demo.ts, PGID 6835)`, which spawned the feed as its own process group (7340) and the deck as its own (7428). `kill -INT 6883` alone (no `pkill`) triggered `stopAll('SIGINT')`; the launcher exited 130, and PIDs 6866/6867/6883/7340/7428 were all gone within 2 seconds. `curl` to 4713 and 3013 afterward both got connection-refused (curl exit 7). No stray processes from the clone survived anywhere on the host. (One unrelated, pre-existing orphaned `next-server`, PID 6593, cwd under a different scratchpad path `wave2-safety/baseline`, predates this rehearsal and is not mine — left untouched, not counted as a gap.) Main checkout confirmed untouched throughout (same PIDs/start-times/head).

### Keyless smoke (step 9)
- Against `packages/util` (143 files): **failed**, exit 1, in 5s. All six departments (`secrets`, `injection`, `access`, `data`, `dependencies`, `platform`) report `"reason": "no certificate after 4 rounds"`. `verifier exit -1: no integration worktree` (integration never ran because no department certified). It wrote a full run tree at `.../keyless-run/`: `stdout.jsonl`, empty `stderr.txt`, `.sessions/` logs, and `repo/` with a git worktree per department — each containing only the base commit's `target.json`/`REPORTING.md`/`verify-safety-report.mjs` and empty `findings/.gitkeep` + `report/.gitkeep` placeholders (no department ever delivered real findings/report content); no `@integration` directory was ever created.
- Confirmed root cause by re-running **with no target** (its coded default, the fixture's own 8-file `sample-target`): **released**, exit 0, in 5s — all six departments `merged`, verifier `exit 0: ok: SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json verified…`, 16 findings written. So `--keyless` itself works correctly; it only works against its own bundled sample target.

### GAPS

1. **`--keyless` silently fails against any target other than the bundled fixture, and this restriction is undocumented outside the script's own header comment.** The usage line (`pnpm run code-safety -- <target path> [--out <dir>] [--model sonnet|opus] [--keyless]`) presents `<target path>` and `--keyless` as freely combinable, and `--keyless` is not mentioned at all in `docs/code-safety-poc.md` or the root `README.md`. A user who tries the natural combination (their own small repo + `--keyless`, to get a free/no-login smoke test) gets, with no warning: `outcome failed in 5s`, all six departments `"reason": "no certificate after 4 rounds"`, and `verifier exit -1: no integration worktree`. Exit code 1, no findings, no report.

2. **The "offline install worked" result does not generalize to a genuinely fresh laptop.** `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` succeeded in 7.6s here only because this host's shared pnpm store was already warm from the main checkout's own earlier install. A user's first-ever clone on a new machine has an empty store and needs network for `pnpm install` regardless of trying `--offline` first; the runbook doesn't mention this distinction (it only says plain `pnpm install`, so this isn't strictly a runbook error, but the offline-first instruction in this rehearsal procedure should not be read as validating true offline capability for a new user).

3. **Minor/cosmetic:** `pnpm install` prints two `[WARN] Failed to create bin ... ENOENT` lines (for `dsh-acp-demo` and `dsh-sdk-jsonrpc-demo`, both unrelated example demo bins whose `lib/bin.js` doesn't exist until after a build). Harmless and unrelated to the code-safety demo path, but a first-time user watching the install may wonder about it since nothing in the runbook mentions expected install warnings.

Everything else the runbook documents for `pnpm run poc` and the LIVE/REPLAY behavior passed exactly as written: the roster count (147/10/124), the forced-build-on-non-default-port behavior, the feed-ready wait, the LIVE and REPLAY badges and footer text, and the single-Ctrl-C/SIGINT clean shutdown of both child servers.

**Screenshot paths** (kept, not cleaned up): `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/scratchpad/wave2-rehearsal/shots/{enterprise,process,safety}.png`, `.../shots-badge/enterprise.png`, `.../shots-replay/replay.png`. Logs and keyless run directories are likewise kept under that same `wave2-rehearsal/` directory; only `fresh/node_modules` and `fresh/apps/command-deck/.next` were removed per step 10.
